subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Pipelines and ETL
description: A fast breakdown of Data Pipelines and ETL for builders.

hook.text: Raw data is messy. It arrives in different formats from dozens of sources. Before analysis, it needs cleaning.

buildup.text: ETL — Extract, Transform, Load — pulls data from sources, cleans and reshapes it, then loads it into a warehouse.

discovery.text: Cloud pipelines like AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, and Dataflow automate ETL at scale.

twist.text: ELT is the new trend: load raw data first, transform later. Cloud warehouses are powerful enough to handle it.

climax.text: A reliable pipeline is the backbone of data-driven decisions. Garbage in, garbage out — pipelines ensure quality.

punchline.text: Clean data in, good decisions out. Pipelines make that happen.

quiz.question: What is the difference between ETL and ELT?
options: ETL transforms data before loading; ELT loads raw data first and transforms later
ETL is for cloud; ELT is for on-premises only
ETL processes data faster than ELT in all cases

details.summary: Data pipelines move and transform data from source systems to analytical destinations. ETL extracts data, transforms it, and loads it into a warehouse. Modern cloud pipelines often use ELT, loading raw data first and transforming it in the warehouse.
details.whyItMatters: Reliable data pipelines are the backbone of every analytics and ML platform. Broken pipelines mean stale dashboards, incorrect reports, and failed model training.
takeaways: ETL transforms data before loading; ELT transforms after loading
Modern cloud pipelines favor ELT with warehouse-side transforms
Pipeline reliability directly affects data-driven decisions

faq.question: What tools are used for cloud data pipelines?
faq.answer: Apache Airflow and managed versions like MWAA and Cloud Composer orchestrate workflows. dbt handles transformation in the warehouse. AWS Glue, Azure Data Factory, and Dataflow provide managed ETL. Fivetran and Airbyte automate source connectors.

faq.question: What is the difference between batch and streaming pipelines?
faq.answer: Batch pipelines process data in scheduled intervals, suitable for daily reports. Streaming pipelines process data continuously in near real-time, necessary for live dashboards and event-driven applications. Many architectures combine both approaches.
